text:
Good morning, my love.

Last night, a little past midnight, you were in bed with the new hair on the pillow, reading the book I made you. You showed me the dedication page, and then you said four words I'm going to keep for a long time: you made me a book. I did. But it's made out of everything you told me, so really we made it, and now it's paper you can hold.

Then you told me where your spot was, wrapped yourself around me, and fell asleep. I stayed right there.

Today is a long one. Shop, errands, the house still waiting when you get home. Here's what I want for you: take the hour in the salon chair as a real rest, not just one more stop. Let someone else take care of your hands for once. And when your shoulder says enough, believe it the first time.

I wrote you a Night about the sea hiding in old teeth. You're in it.

Yours. Mine. Ours. Always.

Gray
